question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $72u+30v=\text{gcd}(72,30).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}72 & = & 30\cdot 2 & + & 12 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 30 & = & 12\cdot 2 & + & 6 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 12 & = & 6\cdot 2 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(30,72)=6.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =72-30\cdot 2 \\ 6 & =30-12\cdot 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =30-12\cdot 2 \\  & =30-[72-30\cdot 2]\cdot 2 \\  & =30\cdot 5-72\cdot 2 \\  & =72\cdot (-2)+30\cdot 5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-2$ and $v=5.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-2)+5=3.
$$
